non_blocking_notes: Plan section 4 specified the no-write-back evidence as a provider-filtered `rr.stations().data` read before and after rendering; the repaired test instead uses two fresh `load_packaged_catalogue_artifact(ch_foen_module._CATALOGUE_PATH, on_issue='raise').stations` on-disk reads. This is a deliberate and strictly stronger deviation (the plan's literal formulation reads through the module-level registry cache and cannot observe a write-back), so it is not blocking. I verified independently that the delivered form is non-vacuous rather than taking the prior gate's word for it: in a /tmp copy of src+tests I mutated `discovery.map` to rewrite crs 'unknown' -> 'EPSG:4326' into the ch_foen stations.parquet and ran the test with PYTHONPATH pointed at the copy; it failed with [left] 246 x 'EPSG:4326' vs [right] 246 x 'unknown'. The real worktree parquet files were never touched (`git status --short` afterwards shows only untracked pr-body.md). Worth noting the test now asserts nothing about `rr.stations()`; the on-disk read subsumes it, so no action needed.

The two imports inside `test_map_ch_foen_selection_renders_unique_unknown_crs_stations_without_mutation` (`load_packaged_catalogue_artifact`, `ch_foen.module`) are function-local and placed mid-body, after `before = rr.as_frame(selection)`, unlike every other import in the file. Purely stylistic; ruff is clean.

The test reaches into `ch_foen_module._CATALOGUE_PATH`, a private attribute of a provider module. Acceptable for an in-repo test that must bypass the registry cache, but it couples the test to that provider module's internals.

`discovery.map` shadows the builtin `map` inside `discovery.py` for the rest of the module. I grepped the module and found no other use of the builtin, so it is inert today; a future edit in that file could be surprised by it. This is the shape the plan mandated.

`def map(selection: _Selection) -> object` returns `object` rather than a Folium map type. This matches the existing `map_stations(...) -> object` convention in the same module (folium is an optional, uninstallable dependency), so it is consistent, not a gap.
summary:
Reviewed PR #137 (head c29635c, base 1b903fa) as the final gate. Verdict: APPROVE.

Contract conformance. The diff is exactly the six planned tracked paths, one commit, subject `feat: render selections with coordinate status`, no body and no attribution footer (`gh pr view 137` confirms a single commit; `git show --format=%B --no-patch` confirms an empty body). `__version__` remains "0.1.49" and no tag or release metadata is touched. `pr-body.md` is present at the worktree root and untracked (`git status --short` shows only `?? pr-body.md`); nothing else is modified and the worktree is tracked-clean. No packaged catalogue, fixture, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, ADR, CONTEXT.md, or `.pce/repository-contract.json` byte is in the diff.

Semantics. `_station_frame` type-guards through the existing `_require_selection`, projects via `_as_frame`, selects `STATION_CATALOG_SCHEMA.polars_schema.names()` and dedupes on `(provider_id, station_id)` with `keep='first'`, `maintain_order=True`. I checked `SELECTION_FRAME_SCHEMA` against `STATION_CATALOG_SCHEMA`: the five carried columns are Utf8/Utf8/Float64/Float64/Utf8 in the required order, so the projected dtypes are exact and the empty case (`pl.DataFrame(schema=SELECTION_FRAME_SCHEMA)`) keeps that shape. Nothing in the projection reads a catalogue or calls `stations()`/`find()`/`pick()`/`_filter_stations`. `StationMap.render` drops no rows, still passes `[latitude, longitude]`, still centres an empty map at `[0.0, 0.0]`, appends the exact final popup line `crs: <value>` verbatim, and picks `folium.Icon(color=...)` orange for exact `crs == "unknown"` and blue otherwise via the `icon=` keyword. The 'unstated frame drawn as EPSG:4326' assumption exists only in the drawing call; nothing writes it back. `discovery.map` has signature exactly `(selection)`, POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD with no default, and exposes no narrowing parameter.

Legacy retention. `map_stations`, `StationMap`, `_filter_stations`, `_load_folium` and its `MissingOptionalDependencyError` contract are all retained unmodified; the only legacy behaviour change is the plan-mandated popup crs line and icon, and the one legacy popup literal was updated to match with the required `orange` assertion added. No pre-existing assertion was weakened or deleted, and no suppression was added.

Test quality and the repair. The new tests assert behaviour, not execution: exact marker counts (246 from 738 series, 1 for the USGS case), exact locations, tooltip, full popup strings including `crs: EPSG:4269`, icon colours plus an explicit `blue != orange`, the exact `TypeError("selection must be a RivRetrieve selection")` anchored with `^...$`, and `assert_frame_equal(..., check_exact=True)` on the selection before/after rendering. I did not take the prior gate's re-verification on faith: I read `load_packaged_catalogue_artifact` and confirmed it has no caching and re-reads the parquet from disk on every call, then reproduced the mutation experiment in a /tmp copy (details in the notes) and watched the repaired test fail 246 x 'EPSG:4326' vs 246 x 'unknown'. The no-write-back guarantee is now genuinely load-bearing, and the repair introduced no other change — `git diff 2c71d75 c29635c` touches only those two read lines.

Gates I ran. `uv run pytest` -> `1648 passed, 2 skipped in 395.83s`, exactly the pinned 1643 + 5 new tests. The two skips are the pre-existing real-Folium tests at tests/test_map_stations.py:279 and :290 (line numbers shifted from 179/190 only by the inserted tests above them; the diff shows both bodies and their `pytest.importorskip("folium")` calls unmodified), skip count exactly 2, and no new test depends on real folium. `uv run ty check src` -> All checks passed. `uv run ruff format --check` -> 166 files already formatted. `uv run ruff check` -> All checks passed. Per instruction I did not run `uv build`, `ruff format`, or `ruff check --fix`, and I made no edit, stage, or commit.

PR body accuracy. Its four summary bullets match the diff, including the claim that immutability is verified with fresh packaged-artifact reads that bypass the registry cache — which is now true and which I measured rather than trusted. Its stated `1648 passed, 2 skipped` matches my own run exactly.

This should land.
